$comment: True (particle) specific gravity of dry glaze materials, for Brongniart's formula. SG is relative to water at 4 °C, so numerically equal to g/cm³. This is the density of the powder's particles as a pycnometer measures it, NOT bulk/tapped density and NOT the SG of a slurry. Master key list: ceramic-materials/ceramics/taxonomy.py (70 keys), generalised beyond the Polish catalogue; see README.md for method, confidence levels and sources.

fields.sg_range: [low, high] seen across grades, sources and natural variation.
fields.confidence: high = pure compound or mineral with a tight published range; medium = natural material or commercial grade whose composition varies; low = estimate with no published figure (frits, stains, blends).
fields.basis: What the value is actually the density of.
fields.solubility: insoluble | slight | soluble. Brongniart assumes all solids stay suspended; dissolved material is not counted correctly (see README).
fields.brongniart: ok | caution (slightly soluble, or highly variable) | invalid (dissolves; the formula does not apply) | n/a (not a glaze solid).

variants.name: Calcined kaolin (metakaolin)
variants.notes: Loses ~14% weight as water on calcining; density depends on calcining temperature (metakaolin ~2.5, spinel/mullite-forming calcines toward 2.63).

materials.name: Ball clay
materials.basis: Kaolinite + illite + quartz + organics; organics pull it down.

materials.name: Bentonite
materials.basis: Montmorillonite; measured density depends on how much interlayer water is left.
materials.notes: Swells and holds water; usually ≤3% of a glaze, so the uncertainty barely matters.

materials.name: Fire clay
materials.basis: Kaolinitic clay with quartz and iron minerals.

materials.name: Terra sigillata (solids)
materials.basis: Fine clay fraction; use the SG of the parent clay if known.
materials.notes: Terra sig is itself a slurry; Brongniart gives its solids per litre directly.

variants.name: Fused / amorphous silica
variants.notes: Much lighter than quartz. Do not confuse with ground quartz.

materials.name: Quartz sand
materials.notes: Coarse grains settle fast; stir thoroughly before weighing a sample.

materials.name: Glass powder (glass meal)
materials.notes: Borosilicate lab glass is ~2.23; lead crystal is 3.0+.

materials.name: Glass granulate / frit chips
materials.notes: Too coarse to stay suspended; a slurry sample will not be representative.

materials.name: Potash feldspar
materials.basis: Orthoclase/microcline (2.55–2.57) plus the free quartz commercial grades carry.

materials.name: Lime feldspar
materials.basis: Anorthite 2.73–2.76; commercial 'lime feldspar' is often a Ca-rich plagioclase and slightly lighter.

materials.name: Nepheline syenite
materials.notes: Very slightly alkaline in water; can make slurries thixotropic over time, but not enough dissolves to affect the formula.

materials.name: Cryolite
materials.notes: ~0.04 g/100 mL — negligible.

materials.name: Lithium carbonate
materials.notes: ~1.3 g/100 mL at 20 °C. In a typical slurry a few grams per litre dissolve; for glazes with >5% Li₂CO₃ expect a small low reading.

variants.name: β-spodumene (calcined)
variants.notes: Calcining expands the structure ~30% by volume; the difference from the natural form is large, so check which one you have.

materials.name: Potassium carbonate (pearl ash)
materials.notes: Dissolves completely (~110 g/100 mL). Also hygroscopic.

materials.name: Soda ash
materials.notes: Dissolves (~30 g/100 mL). At ≤0.5% as a deflocculant the error is negligible; as a flux it is not.

materials.name: Frit (unspecified, lead-free)
materials.notes: Manufacturers' data sheets list relative density as 'no data available'. Alkaline/boron-rich frits sit low (2.4–2.5), calcium/zinc/barium-rich frits high (2.6–2.8).

materials.name: Ferro 3110 (sodium borosilicate, high alkali)
materials.basis: Composition (~70% SiO₂, ~15% Na₂O, some CaO/B₂O₃) is close to soda-lime glass.
materials.notes: Ferro: somewhat soluble; can precipitate in slurries stored a long time.

materials.name: Ferro 3134 (calcium borosilicate)
materials.basis: Estimate from composition (~46% SiO₂, 23% B₂O₃, 20% CaO, 10% Na₂O); high CaO raises it above borosilicate glass.
materials.notes: Boron-rich; known to leach slightly and gel slurries over time. Also sold as Fusion F-2 and 'frit 1042' in parts of Europe.

materials.name: Ferro 3195 (balanced borosilicate)
materials.basis: Estimate from composition (~49% SiO₂, 23% B₂O₃, 12% Al₂O₃, 11% CaO, 6% Na₂O).

materials.name: M 1233 alkaline frit
materials.basis: Estimate for a lead-free high-alkali frit.
materials.notes: High-alkali frits are the most soluble kind.

materials.name: M 6640 alkaline borosilicate frit
materials.basis: Estimate for a lead-free alkaline borosilicate frit.

materials.name: Lead bisilicate frit
materials.notes: Included because lead frits move the mix SG a lot. Handle with appropriate precautions.

materials.name: Gerstley borate
materials.basis: Estimate: colemanite (2.42) + ulexite (1.95) + hectorite-type clay (~2.5). No published figure found.
materials.notes: Slightly soluble and gels slurries over time. Also covers Gerstley substitutes (Gillespie borate, Laguna borate), which differ.

materials.name: Ulexite
materials.notes: More soluble than colemanite; readings drift as it dissolves.

materials.name: Whiting (calcium carbonate)
materials.basis: Calcite. Chalk-based whiting measures the same once pores are wetted.

materials.name: Magnesium carbonate
materials.basis: Light (basic) magnesium carbonate ≈ hydromagnesite, 2.16–2.2; this is the usual ceramic grade.
materials.notes: Ground magnesite (MgCO₃) is 3.0. The fluffy powder is the light grade.

materials.name: Magnesium oxide
materials.notes: Slowly hydrates to Mg(OH)₂ (2.34) in the bucket.

materials.name: Barium carbonate
materials.notes: Toxic; slightly soluble in acids.

materials.name: Talc
materials.basis: Mineral talc; commercial talcs carry chlorite/dolomite/magnesite.

materials.name: Wollastonite
materials.basis: Mineral wollastonite; commercial grades cluster at 2.87–2.9.

materials.name: Zinc oxide
materials.basis: Compound. Calcined and raw ZnO have the same particle density; they differ in bulk density and shrinkage.

materials.name: Bone ash
materials.basis: Hydroxyapatite / tricalcium phosphate. Synthetic bone ash is the upper end.

materials.name: Wood ash
materials.basis: Highly variable: calcium carbonate, silica, potash and phosphate in any proportion.
materials.notes: Unwashed ash contains soluble potash salts, so treat it as invalid. Use washed ash only; measuring your own batch is the only reliable option.

materials.name: Lava / volcanic rock powder
materials.basis: Volcanic rock of varying chemistry; glassy/pumiceous material sits at the low end.
materials.notes: Closed pores in vesicular rock lower the apparent density even when finely ground.

materials.name: Cobalt carbonate
materials.basis: Anhydrous CoCO₃ 4.13. Ceramic grade is usually basic cobalt carbonate, which is lighter.

materials.name: Copper carbonate
materials.basis: Basic copper carbonate ≈ malachite (3.6–4.05). Pure CuCO₃ is not what is sold.

materials.name: Ilmenite
materials.basis: Mineral ilmenite. Granular grades settle fast.

materials.name: Iron chromate
materials.basis: Ceramic 'iron chromate' is a calcined Fe–Cr oxide (spinel/corundum-type), not true FeCrO₄.

materials.name: Iron oxide, red
materials.basis: Hematite / synthetic red iron oxide. Natural grades with clay are lower.

variants.name: Iron oxide, yellow / ochre
variants.notes: Synthetic goethite ~4.0–4.3; natural ochres are clay-diluted and lighter.

materials.name: Manganese dioxide
materials.basis: Pyrolusite. Ore-based grades with gangue (e.g. 'Braunstein' ~80% MnO₂) sit at 4.4–4.8.

materials.name: Nickel oxide, green
materials.notes: 'Black nickel oxide' (non-stoichiometric, higher oxygen) is lighter, ~4.8–6.0.

materials.name: Vanadium pentoxide
materials.notes: ~0.8 g/100 mL. Toxic.

materials.name: Stain (unspecified)
materials.basis: Midpoint of calcined ceramic stains; pick a family from stain_families when known.

materials.name: Titanium dioxide
materials.basis: Anatase 3.84–3.90, rutile 4.23–4.26. Ceramic grades are commonly anatase; check the data sheet.

materials.name: Zircon (zirconium silicate, Zircopax/Superpax)
materials.basis: Mineral zircon 4.6–4.7; milled grades slightly lower.

materials.name: Zirconium oxide
materials.basis: Monoclinic baddeleyite; stabilised grades up to 6.1.

materials.name: Kiln separator / mould release
materials.notes: Not a glaze solid.

materials.name: Binder (gum arabic, CMC)
materials.notes: Dissolves. At the usual 0.1–1% the error is small; leave it out of the mix SG.

materials.name: Deflocculant (Darvan, sodium silicate, Dolaflux)
materials.notes: Dissolved additive; exclude from the mix SG.

materials.name: Epsom salt (flocculant)
materials.notes: Dissolves; at flocculant doses (≤0.2%) it is negligible. Exclude from the mix SG.

materials.name: Glaze additives (suspenders, hardeners)
materials.notes: Proprietary; usually small and partly soluble. Exclude.

materials.name: Plaster
materials.notes: Sets in water; not a glaze material.

stain_families.$comment: Calcined inorganic stains, by crystal host. Manufacturers do not publish density; values are the host crystal's density, slightly reduced for the silica/flux carriers stains are milled with. All confidence: low. In practice stains are 1–10% of a glaze, so ±0.4 here moves the mix SG by <1%.

zircon.name: Zircon-based (Zr–V blue/turquoise, Zr–Pr yellow, Zr–Fe coral/pink, inclusion reds/oranges)

colour_hint.$comment: Rough guide from colour name to family, for when only the colour is known. Not reliable for a specific product.
